items.rationale: Any split that would leave fewer than min_samples_leaf training samples in a child is not allowed, so leaves average more rows and predictions smooth out. Confusing it with the minimum samples needed to split a node (min_samples_split) is a typical slip.

Each row is predicted only by the trees whose bootstrap sample left it out, so the OOB score estimates generalization from the training rows alone. Option c describes a held-out test set; OOB needs no separate set, and option b is training error.
n_estimators is the number of trees fitted and averaged into the forest's prediction. Option a describes the bootstrap sample size, a different quantity and the likeliest mix-up.

RMSE is the square root of the mean squared error: a typical error size in the target's units that penalizes large misses more. Option c is mean absolute error, which counts every miss equally; option a is R², which is unit-free.

Leaves of one row mean each tree fits noise, so raising min_samples_leaf regularizes each tree and should raise the OOB score. More trees (option a) only reduce the variance of the average, not the noise each tree fits, and raising max_features (option c) makes trees more alike, weakening the averaging.

For B trees of variance s2 and pairwise correlation r, the average has variance r*s2 + (1-r)*s2/B = 0.5*4 + 0.5*4/100 = 2 + 0.02 = 2.02. An answer of 0.04 assumes uncorrelated trees; correlation puts a floor of r*s2 = 2 under the variance, which is why more trees stop helping and why lowering max_features helps.

Choosing the best of 60 settings by test score makes the test rows part of model selection, so the winning score is biased upward. Option c is wrong because the averaging does not protect against selection on the test rows, and option d is wrong because how the settings were chosen is exactly what causes the bias.
Squared errors are 1, 4, 4 and 16, summing to 25; the mean is 6.25 and its square root is 2.5 thousand dollars. An answer of 6.25 forgets the square root, and 2.25 is the mean absolute error.

The best score is 0.873, so the forest must reach at least 0.871; 100 trees scores 0.868 and misses, 400 trees scores 0.872 and is the cheapest that qualifies. Option d pays four times the cost of 400 trees for 0.001.
